fields.example: Irish uses Verb-Subject-Object order: verb comes first. 'Tá' = 'am/is/are'.
Questions use 'An' at the start. 'An bhfuil tú go maith?' = 'Are you well?'
Negative of 'tá'. 'Níl mé tuirseach.' = 'I am not tired.'
Standard greeting. Response: 'Dia is Muire duit.'
Also: 'Slán leat' (said to the person leaving), 'Slán agat' (said by the person leaving).
Lit. 'with your will'. Goes at the end of a request.

fields.translation: Thank you (lit. may you have good)
fields.example: Often shortened in speech. Response: 'Tá fáilte romhat.'
Informal. Formal: 'Conas atá sibh?' (to a group).

fields.original: Tá mé go maith, go raibh maith agat.
fields.pronunciation: taw may guh mah, guh rev mah agut
fields.example: Natural full response to 'Conas atá tú?'
Used to get attention or apologise.
'Is maith liom seo.' (I like this.) 'Cad é sin?' (What is that?)
'Tá mé anseo.' (I am here.) 'Tá sé ansin.' (It is there.)

fields.original: an ceann seo / an ceann sin
fields.pronunciation: un kyown shuh / un kyown shin
fields.example: 'Ó, an ceann seo, le do thoil.' (Oh, this one, please.)
'Tá mé tuirseach.' (I am tired.) Irish has no single infinitive — 'bí' is the base form.

fields.translation: I want / I need (lit. it is needed from me)
fields.example: 'Teastaíonn uisce uaim.' (I want/need water.) Irish expresses want differently to English.

fields.translation: I like (lit. it is good with me)
fields.example: 'Is maith liom caife.' (I like coffee.)
'Tá a fhios agam.' (I know.) 'Níl a fhios agam.' (I don't know.)
'Téim go Gaillimh.' (I go to Galway.)
'Ba mhaith liom caife, le do thoil.' (I'd like a coffee, please.)

fields.original: An féidir leat ... a thabhairt dom?
fields.pronunciation: un fay-dir lyat ... ah how-irt dum
fields.example: 'An féidir leat uisce a thabhairt dom?' (Can you give me water?)
'Cá bhfuil an leithreas?' (Where is the toilet?)
'An bhfuil seomra agat?' (Do you have a room?)

fields.original: Cad é an focal Gaeilge ar...?
fields.pronunciation: kod ay un fuk-ul gway-lge er
fields.translation: What is the Irish word for...?
fields.example: 'Cad é an focal Gaeilge ar 'water'?' (What is the Irish for 'water'?)
Say this freely — it will earn respect from native speakers.

fields.original: An féidir leat é sin a rá arís?
fields.pronunciation: un fay-dir lyat ay shin ah raw ah-reesh
fields.example: Polite repeat request.
Irish speakers will almost always accommodate.

fields.original: Cad é a chiallaíonn sé sin?
fields.pronunciation: kod ay ah hee-ah-leen shay shin
fields.example: Point at text or repeat a word you heard.
Universally understood. People are happy to help Irish learners.
